title: Google Cloud: a refusal that names the wrong person, and a relay name that answers publicly
synthetic: Fictional teaching case for Cinderline Components. Names, addresses, account and project identifiers and every error text are invented; nothing was deployed or observed. The region us-east4 and the relay name follow the module's worked example.

deployment.value: Classic workspace in project cl-dbx-prod (us-east4) with back-end Private Service Connect; classic job clusters

Customer-managed VPC cl-vpc-dbx in host project cl-net-host; node subnet dbx-nodes-use4 (10.20.0.0/22); endpoint subnet dbx-psc-use4 (10.20.8.0/28) with relay-pe (10.20.8.2) and workspace-pe (10.20.8.3); users' transit network cl-vpc-transit. The Cloud NAT was removed when PSC was enabled
external location loc_quality_raw on gs://cl-quality-raw/inspections/ through storage credential cred_quality; table quality.raw.inspections

evidence.capture: The exact error or symptom text, its time, the run or cluster ID, and which service answered (or that none did)
evidence.where: The job run or cluster event log
evidence.doesNotProve: Which layer is at fault until the service that answered, if any, has been named

evidence.capture: The job's run-as principal as its settings show it
evidence.doesNotProve: That the principal holds any privilege, or anything about the network

evidence.capture: SHOW GRANTS on the catalog, the schema and the table, read for the acting principal and its groups
evidence.doesNotProve: Anything about storage permissions or reachability

evidence.capture: DESCRIBE STORAGE CREDENTIAL cred_quality: the service account email
evidence.doesNotProve: Which bucket roles that email holds

evidence.capture: The bucket's IAM policy, read for that email
evidence.doesNotProve: Policies inherited from the project, folder or organization

evidence.capture: Policy Troubleshooter for that email, storage.objects.get and the bucket, with the inherited policies it consulted
The relay name's answer from a VM in dbx-nodes-use4, with time
evidence.where: A VM or running cluster in the node subnet
evidence.doesNotProve: That the endpoint is accepted or that a firewall rule admits the flow

evidence.capture: The managed zone's private visibility networks and its A records

evidence.doesNotProve: That the name resolves to it

evidence.capture: Egress firewall rules for the node network sorted by priority, and any firewall policies attached above the VPC

symptoms.title: The nightly job is refused in someone else's name
symptoms.observed: PERMISSION_DENIED: User ana@cinderline.example does not have SELECT on table quality.raw.inspections
symptoms.context: Ana created quality_nightly. The design says the job acts as sp-quality-nightly, which holds its grants through the quality-jobs group.

symptoms.title: Cluster starts stall after back-end PSC was enabled
symptoms.observed: Cluster start stalled and failed; the node never opened its secure tunnel; no principal, permission or constraint appears in any error
symptoms.context: This week back-end Private Service Connect was enabled and the Cloud NAT removed. Zone dbx-psc-zone was created at the same time.

unknowns.question: Whether serverless compute can reach private resources in Cinderline's VPC on Google Cloud
unknowns.whyUnknown: The sources read for the module conflict: provider documentation lists the NCC binding for AWS and Azure only, while an SDK models a Google Cloud field; a field in a schema is not availability

unknowns.whyUnknown: Not settled by the sources the module read
